description: Implement the manual global price sync mechanism. This includes: (1) a sync signal service using a Firestore document 'meta/syncSignal' that the admin writes to when triggering a sync, (2) a real-time onSnapshot listener on the employee HomePage that watches this signal document and auto-refreshes prices when it changes, (3) a 'Sync Prices to All Devices' button in the AdminPage under the product management section, and (4) CSS styling for the new button.
steps: Step 1: Create a new service file src/services/syncService.js that exports two functions: (a) triggerGlobalSync() - writes a new timestamp to Firestore doc 'meta/syncSignal' with field {lastSyncAt: Date.now(), triggeredBy: 'admin'}. This is what the admin button calls. (b) onSyncSignalChange(callback) - sets up an onSnapshot listener on 'meta/syncSignal' and calls the callback whenever the document changes (skip the initial snapshot to avoid unnecessary refetch on page load). Returns an unsubscribe function. Import {doc, setDoc, onSnapshot} from 'firebase/firestore' and {db} from './firebase.js'.

Step 2: Modify src/pages/AdminPage.jsx to add a 'Sync Prices to All Devices' button. Add it as a new admin-card section positioned AFTER the ProductEditor and BEFORE the admin-grid (CSV import/export). Import triggerGlobalSync from syncService.js. The button should: show a confirmation dialog ('Push latest prices to all employee devices?'), call triggerGlobalSync(), show a toast success message ('Prices synced to all devices'), handle errors with toast.error. Include state for isSyncing to disable the button during the operation. The section should have a heading 'Price Sync' with explanatory text 'Push the latest prices to all currently connected employee devices.'

Step 3: Modify src/pages/HomePage.jsx to listen for sync signals. Import onSyncSignalChange from syncService.js. In a new useEffect (separate from the existing data load effect), call onSyncSignalChange with a callback that: (a) clears the localStorage cache key 'pricelist_catalog_cache', (b) calls fetchCatalogWithCache() to get fresh data, (c) updates the products state via setProducts(prepareProductsForSearch(freshProducts)), (d) shows a toast notification 'Prices updated' so the user knows new prices arrived. The useEffect should return the unsubscribe function for cleanup. Use a ref (useRef) to skip the first onSnapshot callback (the initial snapshot fires immediately on subscription - we only want to react to subsequent changes).

Step 4: Add CSS styles to src/styles.css for the sync button section. Add a .sync-section class with appropriate styling that matches the existing admin-card pattern. Add a .sync-button class styled distinctively (use a green/teal color like #0f766e background, white text) to make it visually distinct from regular buttons and convey 'push/broadcast' semantics. Also add a .sync-description class for the explanatory text (color: #667085, font-size: 13px, margin: 0).
acceptance_criteria: A new file src/services/syncService.js exists with triggerGlobalSync() and onSyncSignalChange() functions
AdminPage.jsx shows a 'Sync Prices to All Devices' button in a distinct section between ProductEditor and the CSV grid
Clicking the sync button calls triggerGlobalSync() which writes to Firestore 'meta/syncSignal'
HomePage.jsx sets up an onSnapshot listener on 'meta/syncSignal' that triggers a price refresh when the document changes
The initial onSnapshot callback is skipped (no unnecessary refetch on page load)
The onSnapshot listener is properly cleaned up on component unmount
The project builds without errors (npm run build succeeds)
No automatic sync occurs on price edit - only the manual button triggers global sync
verification: Run 'npm run build' in /projects/sandbox/pricelist and confirm exit code 0 with no errors
Verify src/services/syncService.js exists and exports triggerGlobalSync and onSyncSignalChange
Verify AdminPage.jsx imports and uses triggerGlobalSync
Verify HomePage.jsx imports and uses onSyncSignalChange with proper cleanup
findings: All 4 steps implemented successfully. Build passes with exit code 0. The chunk size warning (596KB > 500KB) is pre-existing and not caused by this change. No test framework exists so build success is the verification.
